etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French myriade, from Late Latin mȳriadem (accusative of mȳrias), from Ancient Greek μυριάς (muriás, “number of 10,000”), from μυρίος (muríos, “numberless, countless, infinite”). By surface analysis, myria- +‎ -ad.
senses: A countless number or multitude (of specified things) [from 16th c.]
(modifying a singular noun) Multifaceted, having innumerable elements. [from 18th c.]
(modifying a plural noun) Great in number; innumerable, multitudinous. [from 18th c.]
